transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hi Ms. Tremblay, thanks for coming back in to see me.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't really have much time. I have to get back to base.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I wanted to talk to you about the follow-up instructions we gave you when you were discharged yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Right. The clinic appointment. There is a problem with it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yeah, it looks like there was some confusion with the paperwork regarding where you were sent.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I tried to call them this morning. They told me they don't take my insurance. Tricare isn't accepted there.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry. My team and I made a mistake in how we coordinated your care. We should have verified the provider's network before putting it in your discharge papers.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care whose fault it is. I just don't have an appointment and I need to get this cleared up so I can get back to work.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that this is frustrating. You're just trying to get back to your duties and now you have to deal with this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Exactly. So what happens now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are looking into it. We just need to find another spot that works.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will I know? I can't just stay in limbo.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not sure yet, but we'll probably get an email out to you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: An email? When? Today? Tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll have to check with the coordinator. Just stay tuned for an update.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That isn't a plan. I need a date and a time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know, and I'm sorry for the mix-up. It was our error. But the system for scheduling is a bit slow on Tuesdays.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't need to know about the system. I need to know who is treating me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, we'll see what we can do. I just need to—

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm sorry, you're interrupting me. I'm telling you that my commanding officer needs my medical clearance by Friday.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to go in a couple of minutes for rounds, so let's wrap this up. I'll definitely look into a new clinic.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're leaving? Now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, but I've heard your concern. We'll figure out a way to get you seen.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unacceptable. You're telling me you messed up my referral and now you're telling me to wait for an email that might not come until tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize this is an inconvenience. I'll do my best to get it sorted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's not an inconvenience, it's a failure in the process.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I agree, we dropped the ball here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what is the actual next step?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, I'll check with the staff. We'll get back to you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a specific step. Do I call someone? Do I go somewhere?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just wait for the update.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is a waste of my time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I apologize again for the mistake. I really do.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Your apology doesn't get me a doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I'll try to make it happen quickly.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language ('let's wrap this up') and interrupts the patient's explanation of their deadline.

E.justification: The error is named explicitly, but there are no comprehension checks performed throughout the interaction.

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language, takes responsibility for the team, and maintains accountability despite patient pushback.

R.justification: Resident names a specific emotion ('frustrating') and references the patient's desire to return to their duties.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders ('stay tuned', 'we'll figure out a way') without specific steps, timelines, or patient roles.
